standard.title: Aluminium Alloy Tube for Irrigation Purposes — Specification, Part 2: Extruded Tube (Second Revision)
standard.sector: Metallurgical Engineering / Light Metals and their Alloys

sectional_committee.name: Light Metals and their Alloys Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the material composition, mechanical properties, dimensions, tolerances, and testing schedules for extruded aluminium alloy tubes designed for agricultural and sprinkler irrigation networks. It covers tubes suitable for a maximum continuous working pressure of 1 000 kN/m² (10 kgf/cm²) for nominal outer diameters up to and including 200 mm.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the material composition, mechanical properties, dimensions, tolerances, and testing schedules for extruded aluminium alloy tubes designed for agricultural and sprinkler irrigation networks. It covers tubes suitable for a maximum continuous working pressure of 1 000 kN/m² (10 kgf/cm²) for nominal outer diameters up to and including 200 mm.

amendments.summary: Modifies basic dimensional tolerances, tube sizes, and structural parameters under Table 2.

Substitutes the mathematical tolerance formula in Table 2, Column 3. It replaces the legacy multiplication-based factor '1/2 (AA*BB) . (d)^2' with the corrected addition-based factor '1/2 (AA+BB) . (d)^2' (where d is the nominal wall thickness of the extruded tube) to rectify an algebraic error in the eccentricity calculation.

qco.name: Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Extruded Aluminium Alloy Tubes for Irrigation Purposes must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, stocking, or distributing uncertified irrigation tubes in India is a punishable offense under the BIS Act, 2016. Micro and small scale units are granted specific delayed compliance phases, and export shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial alloy tubes.
requirements: Every extruded tube must be legibly and indelibly marked on its outer surface with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 7092 Part 2).
The extruded tubes are specified to safely withstand a maximum continuous hydrostatic working pressure of 1 000 kN/m² (10 kgf/cm²) during field operations.

Tubes must be manufactured from designated corrosion-resistant wrought aluminium alloys (typically unified grades 63400-WP or 64430-WP, formerly HE9-WP or HE30-WP) to resist both dynamic water pressure and corrosive agricultural soils.

The ladle analysis of the alloy must be strictly controlled (limiting iron, silicon, copper, manganese, zinc, titanium, and magnesium impurities) to guarantee correct material temper, strength, and corrosion-resistance behavior.
Specimens cut from finished extruded tubes must undergo tensile testing per IS 2657 to demonstrate ultimate tensile strength (UTS) values matching the specified temper of the selected alloy.

Tubes must demonstrate high structural yield behavior, satisfying specified 0.2% proof strength boundaries and exhibiting a mandatory minimum elongation percentage over a standard 50 mm gauge length to prevent structural cracking.

The extruded tube must demonstrate high ductility under localized mechanical expansion. A tapered metal drift must be driven into the end of a conditioned specimen to expand the nominal outside diameter by a specified percentage without exhibiting any signs of cracking or splitting.
Tubes must undergo hydrostatic pressure testing at the factory, showing zero water weeping, joint leaks, pinholes, or permanent physical swelling under test pressure.

Extruded tube diameters and wall thicknesses must satisfy the strict limits of Table 2. Under Amendment No. 2, the eccentricity tolerance of the tube walls is calculated using the corrected mathematical formula: 1/2 (AA+BB) . (d)^2 (where d is the nominal wall thickness).
